title: DEC-240 (a4): make the flagless call-site count see an aliased, re-exported or out-of-tree caller
description:
Follow-up to LCLI-768, filed from rv330-lcli685-final's single LOW under DEC-240 (a6): a LOW from the final pass does not block the landing, it is filed and named. That pass approved opum-ai/lore-cli#685 at ffaff04d, which landed on dev as dcdff128.

THE GAP, in the reviewer's terms: the (a4) call-site count in test/ci-hardening.test.ts is lexical on the identifier `flaglessGlobalInstall(`, so a third caller can dodge it — an import alias (`import { flaglessGlobalInstall as f }` then `f(...)`), a re-export under another name, a reference assigned to a variable or `.call`/`.apply`, or any caller outside benchmark/, scripts/ and docker/, for example src/, which loadSources does not walk. Each needs a deliberate rename or a caller in an unusual place, and the count over-counts rather than under-counts on odd declaration spacing, so it fails closed there. It is therefore a hardening item, not a live hole: DEC-240 (a4)'s one-exception rule is currently enforced for the shapes anyone is likely to write.

WHY IT MATTERS AT ALL: the count is what stops a third caller from inheriting the (a4) exception to "npm install carries --ignore-scripts". A caller that dodged the count would also lose the npm-major-12 gate and the config positive control, which live in qualify() rather than in the helper — the helper's own guards (absolute path, containment by realpath, two allowed extras, merged-env readback) still hold, so the exposure is the script-approval policy rather than arbitrary installs.

A FIX would also flag any import of flaglessGlobalInstall outside its own file that renames it, or that comes from a file not on a known list. Recorded here rather than done in the r3 round because DEC-240 (a6) closed that round at the three items it named.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A caller that imports flaglessGlobalInstall under another name, re-exports it under another name, or holds it in a variable and calls that, is counted by the call-site check, and a test proves each of those shapes goes red when a third one exists.
A caller placed outside benchmark/, scripts/ and docker/ is counted, or the scan gap is named in the check with the reason it is acceptable.
The real tree still reports exactly two call sites, so the tightening does not redden the current sources.
